prize_parts.citation: For developing empirical methods to estimate demand and market power in differentiated-product industries with endogenous prices.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged, but I have narrowed the citation. In round 1 it also mentioned competition and Pakes's dynamic-industry work. After the chair's question about whether demand estimation and dynamic oligopoly form one coherent discovery, I judge that the cleanest credit rests on the demand and market-power estimator alone. Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (1995) solved a concrete identification problem: recovering substitution patterns and markups from market-level data when prices are endogenous and products are differentiated. The solution is about thirty years old and has been re-implemented, criticised and extended in many settings. It is routine in merger review and regulatory counterfactuals, and it spread into trade, health, environmental and transport economics. That is evidence that the method changed what can be measured and decided, not merely that it is technically elegant. Pakes is the natural anchor and also supplies the dynamic-industry line, but I no longer rely on that line to justify the prize. I do not apply a lower bar to a methods contribution than to a discovery-based one. The test is the same for both: what became knowable, how credible the identification is, whether the result has been confirmed and used, and whether credit can be assigned exactly. On that test I still find B045 more clearly attributable than B009 and less exposed to priority disputes than B014.
statement.case_against: I should be candid about the weaknesses. First, I am the only member who prefers B045, and that count is not evidence of merit or of demerit. It does tell me this case would need several members to be persuaded on the merits, and the exchange so far has not done that. Second, attribution is not free of trouble. The three-name cap leaves out Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin. Bresnahan's earlier structural work on market power and product differentiation is an independent contribution, and a committee could regard the BLP trio as a later, narrower implementation of a larger agenda. Third, the case is mainly methodological, and some colleagues reasonably want a stronger link to a finding about the world. Identification and instrument-validity critiques of BLP-type estimators are real, although they have refined the approach and not displaced it. Fourth, B014 and B009 are mature and have wider support, and the B009 supporters have credible answers on replication and policy reach. I do not think the B045 case is stronger on scientific merit than all of that. I think it is competitive and better bounded in attribution, and I hold that with moderate confidence.

responses.point: Friberg ranked B014 first and B045 third. He said he does not think the BLP case is weaker on scientific merit, but he prefers B014 because its credited core is more cleanly defined under the two-to-three-name constraint.
responses.response: I accept the substance of this. We largely agree on merit, and the disagreement is about which core is better bounded. I do not think B014 is cleaner. Melitz and Helpman are an obvious pair, but the uncredited priority claims of Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, and the Arkolakis-Costinot-Rodriguez-Clare qualification on welfare gains, are a similar order of problem to Bresnahan's claim for B045. The difference is that the BLP estimator has a single identifiable origin paper with exactly three authors, whereas the heterogeneous-firm framework rests on a cluster of near-simultaneous contributions. I would not overstate this. Reasonable members can weigh the two attribution problems differently, and I list B014 as my first alternative for that reason.

responses.point: Teorell prefers Autor, Hanson and Dorn for the China-shock evidence, and he treats Katz's wage-structure work as a parallel contribution whose credit boundary is contestable.
responses.response: I think your framing shows why B009 is harder to settle than its support count suggests. The committee has to decide first what the discovery is, and the answer determines whether Dorn or Katz is named. Both trios have strong defenders, and each side concedes a real cost. I take that as a reason to stay at B045 as the more settled attribution, not as a verdict against B009. If the committee defined the B009 discovery as the China-shock evidence, I would find your trio the most accurate and a credible alternative. I would then weigh the open debate on shift-share inference and persistence against the settled record of BLP. I have not changed my view that B009 is a strong candidate.

responses.point: Boppart prefers B014 and argues that its attribution is cleaner because the credited discovery is a single framework. He would word the citation around selection and reallocation to meet the priority objections of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum.
responses.response: I agree that wording the citation around selection and reallocation narrows the priority problem. It does not remove it, because you concede that the committee must decide whether Melitz's model is distinct from the Bernard-Eaton-Kortum line, and I cannot settle that from the evidence we have. I apply the same discipline to B045: I narrowed my citation to demand and market-power estimation, so that it does not claim the wider structural-IO programme. Symmetry matters here. If a narrowly worded citation is an adequate answer for B014, it is also an adequate answer for the Bresnahan question on B045. That is the main reason I do not move to B014.

responses.point: Hassler, as chair, moved from B040 to B009 with Autor, Hanson and Katz. He argues that the technology and trade strands are one achievement, that the evidence is replicated, and that the citation must avoid claiming the task theory. He accepts Dorn for Katz as a defensible variant.
responses.response: Your move shows the committee is converging on B009's quality, and I agree that its evidence is mature. I do not agree that a single-achievement reading removes the attribution problem. Your own uncertainty list asks whether the technology and trade strands are one achievement or two, and you accept Dorn as a defensible substitute. You also note that Katz appears in B050 and that credit division is unsettled. Those are the issues I weigh against B009 on attribution. I accept your reading of the citation, which should rest on empirical labour-demand evidence and not on task theory, and I would want the same discipline in any B009 text. This is why I keep B009 as a serious alternative and not as a lesser option.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would treat Bresnahan's earlier work as a distinct claim strong enough to require his inclusion, and whether replacing Levinsohn with Bresnahan would break the clean attribution of the BLP estimator. I think it would, but I cannot establish it from the evidence supplied.
Whether a citation limited to demand and market-power estimation is a fair description of what Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn did, or whether it understates Pakes's dynamic-industry contribution.
Whether the committee will weigh a methodological advance by the same criteria as a discovery-based candidate, or will want a clearer finding about the world.

Whether the B009 discovery can be defined and credited convincingly, or whether the priority and welfare-gain questions in B014 can be resolved by narrow wording. Either would make one of my alternatives the stronger prize.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to any credited B045 name is apparent from the supplied profile. The profile documents an SSE affiliation shared with committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and co-authored COVID policy work with SSE economists. These are collegial ties and not links to any candidate. My own work is in matching, auctions and market design, with co-authors such as Svensson, Ehlers, Biró, Teytelboym and Trapp, none of whom is credited on B045, B014 or B009. I am a member of KVA and IVA according to my own CV and homepage, which have not been checked against KVA's list. I disclose these connections and do not adjudicate them, and I claim no independent verification.
